# Compacted Summary: Chapter 1 (Complete and Final – Updated 32)

## Setting and Time
- **Season/Period**: Spring through late August, then Christmas/New Year period of first year; now nearly three weeks into new year (1832)
- **Primary Location**: Middlemarch and surrounding areas (Lowick, the Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Wilhaven, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Salmere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley)
- **Atmospheric Details**: Baker's boy frequently late; wind off water with salt and tar smell; dog barking periodically; bees in lavender behind parsonage; gulls quarreling over fish heads; carts with turnips; frost silvering hedges; road rutted and puddled after thaw; children chasing hoops down lane; bell for vespers ringing thinly; chalk sun on forge wall; smoke from chimneys lying flat over fields; light going early at end of August; starlit darkness; frosty air in late year; rain threatening since morning but holding off
- **Secondary Characters/Background**: Ilrine Corrett (herbalist), Eldette Corrett (cooper), Thidrek Corrett (smith), Ridan Corrett (glazier), Jotho Corrett; Aessa Hollwood (ferryman), Cotho Hollwood (mason), Halan Hollwood (shepherd), Ulvie Hollwood (weaver), Thiena Hollwood (glazier); Elnar Brackwood (weaver), Senelle Brackwood (ferryman), Jovus Brackwood (miller), Madan Brackwood (scribe), Cotho Brackwood (shepherd), Tassa Brackwood (weaver); Colan Lindson (born at Quenwick), Islis Lindson (shepherd, born at Quenwick), Movie Lindson (weaver), Maric Lindson (mason, born at Quenwick, called "Old Maric"); Ridette Lindson (tanner); Orrine Stenworth (mason); Feena Stenworth (miller); Rira Stenworth (cooper, born at Wilhaven); Mrs. Abel (housekeeper at Stone Court), Mr. Abel; Mrs. Dollop (spirited landlady of Tankard in Slaughter Lane); Mr. Dill (barber); Fletcher (Hawley's clerk, has bad finger)

## Main Characters

**Dorothea**
- Recently widowed; residing at Lowick Manor
- Strong admiration for Caleb Garth's work knowledge; hopes to improve land and build good cottages
- Final Grange encounter: Will declared best is over, would live like one who saw heaven in trance
- Mistakenly believed Will's words referred to Mrs. Lydgate; experienced certainty his conduct with Rosamond should be above suspicion
- Though thought she might be what Will cared for most, doubt overcame this; credited all to friendship and obstruction from Casaubon's codicil
- Saw Will with portfolio on road; felt pang leaving him behind; wished they could have been happy thinking of each other
- Forced to keep money under Casaubon's codicil that ought to have been Will's, causing distress
- **Bulstrode's Report**: Described as "a woman of most munificent disposition" in possession of funds she can well spare; has destined chief part of funds to another purpose; willing to consider taking Bulstrode's place in relation to Hospital; wishes ample time to mature thoughts; setting out on journey into Yorkshire with Sir James and Lady Chettam; her decision regarding Hospital contribution will depend on conclusions about land she is to see there

**Will Ladislaw**
- Spoke impetuously at Grange about what forbidden him by own pride and honor
- Passionate love for Dorothea which he forbade himself to utter; what kept him silent was that she was forced to keep money that ought to have been his
- After parting: certainty had much more bitterness; had no assurance she loved him
- Still at Middlemarch despite weeks since parting; frequenting Lydgate's household; warbling continually with Rosamond (scandal spreading per Mrs. Cadwallader)
- Raffles knows connection between Will and Bulstrode but deliberately conceals this as card to play
- Father was at Boulogne very ill; mother's family engaged in "respectable thieving line"; mother (Sarah) ran away after Archie Duncan rejected her
- Rejected Bulstrode's money; stated unblemished honor and unstained birth important; recognized stain through mother; refuses "ill-gotten money"; departed with determined quickness
- Wrote brief letter to Dorothea asking permission to call at Lowick
- **Public Scandal**: His genealogy now public knowledge in Middlemarch via Bambridge's disclosure at Green Dragon; described as having "queer genealogy"—high-spirited young lady (Dorothea's aunt), musical Polish patriot, with "grafting of the Jew pawnbroker" (Bulstrode's pawnbroker business connection); scandal raises questions about his legitimacy and inheritance rights, though legally cannot be proven to affect his claims; townspeople conjecture freely about his background

**Caleb Garth**
- Met Bulstrode regarding stable drainage at Stone Court
- Working with railroads: measured and valued outlying piece of land at Yoddrell's farm belonging to Lowick Manor; confronted laborers preparing to interfere with railroad agents
- Decided to take Fred Vincy on as assistant with desk-work and accounts; offered eighty pounds for first year, more after
- **Stone Court Opportunity**: Consulted by Bulstrode on farm management; advised against mere bailiff, recommended yearly letting of land, stock, and implements with proportionate share of proceeds; alluring idea occurred to Caleb—what if Fred Vincy could be placed at Stone Court under Caleb's management responsibility? Would be excellent schooling for Fred
- **Critical Moral Moment with Raffles**: Took up Raffles in his gig after Raffles got down from coach; Raffles had recognized Caleb from previous meeting at Stone Court with Bulstrode; Caleb saw Raffles was ill and provided shelter
- **Final Confrontation with Bulstrode—Moral Firmness**: When Bulstrode attempted to continue business arrangement, Caleb made firm declaration: must request Bulstrode put business into other hands; must give it up because obliged to believe Raffles has told him truth about Bulstrode's harmful past life (Bulstrode led harmful life for gain, kept others out of their rights by deceit); can't be happy working with Bulstrode or profiting by him; hurts his mind
- **Merciful Resolution**: When Bulstrode tried further appeals, Caleb waved him off with merciful intention; stated what Raffles told him will never pass from his lips unless something unknown forces it from him; acknowledged if Bulstrode repents for keeping others out of their rights by deceit, he must want to go back but can't—that must be bitter; not for Caleb to make life harder; stated he doesn't judge as wicked or righteous, doesn't know everything; a man may do wrong and his will may rise clear out of it, though he can't get his life clear; that's bad punishment; if it is so with Bulstrode, Caleb is very sorry but has feeling inside he can't go on working with him; promised good-day

**Mary Garth**
- Staying at Lowick Rectory with Miss Farebrother and Mrs. Farebrother
- Told Farebrother: "I have too strong a feeling for Fred to give him up for any one else"
- Upon Fred telling her of engagement with her father, touched keenly; scolded him for not seeing Farebrother's delicate feeling
- Earnestly desired to be clear she loved Fred best; determined to watch over her affections and constancy
- Currently telling stories to children at Lowick Parsonage (Rumpelstiltskin tale); Fred seated near her, watching with admiration

**Fred Vincy**
- Age four-and-twenty; son of Mr. Vincy; rejected Church vocation; took degree
- Encountered Caleb Garth at Yoddrell's farm; accepted eighty pounds for first year, more after
- Mr. Vincy responded with profound surprise and cutting disappointment; will keep no horse for Fred
- Casually mentioned to Rosamond what he heard about Casaubon's codicil mentioning Ladislaw
- Acknowledged debt to Caleb which will never be discharged
- At Lowick Parsonage: seated near Mary during storytelling; watching her with admiration
- Billiard room incident: encountered Lydgate gambling; felt shock; old opinion of Lydgate as prig reversed
- **Farebrother's Intervention and Warning**: Farebrother drew Fred aside at St. Botolph's; confessed temptation to let Fred go wrong; disclosed satisfaction of Fred's affections stands in way of his own; warned Mary's affection is "conditionally bound" and liable to change; Fred seized by uncomfortable chill; tone changed to encouraging; Farebrother spoke of returning to old intention and uttering warning; moment produced regenerating effect in Fred

**Mr. Lydgate**
- Doctor/physician; age nine-and-twenty
- **Financial Crisis**: Debt amounts to three hundred and eighty pounds at Brassing; creditor Mr. Dover holds bill of sale on furniture; Dover's agent put a man in Lydgate's house
- **Gambling Incident and Aftermath**: Played at billiard-table; won repeatedly but ended by losing four to five pounds overall; felt unmixed disgust next day
- **Bulstrode's Financial Offer—Accepted**: Bulstrode offered thousand pounds to free him from burdens; Lydgate accepted this offer; received cash to pay Dover's agent
- **Emotional Conflict About the Loan**: As he canted home with good news for Rosamond, thought crossed his mind with unpleasant impression "as from a dark-winged flight of evil augury"—contrast in himself which few months had brought; he should be overjoyed at being under strong personal obligation but was uneasy; loan felt more vividly present than ever; relation of personal indebtedness to Bulstrode was what he had once been most resolved to avoid; worried Bulstrode's motives for sudden beneficence following chillest indifference might be merely selfish; knew delicate history of loan but could not tell it to others
- **Arrived at Stone Court Morning of Raffles's Death**: Arrived at half-past ten in time to witness final pause of breath; when entering room, Bulstrode observed sudden expression in Lydgate's face showing recognition that he had not judged correctly; Lydgate stood by bed in silence, eyes turned on dying man, with subdued activity of expression showing inward debate
- **Uneasy About Case**: This morning was in state of recovered hope and freedom; had set out on work with all old animation; felt himself strong enough to bear all deficiencies of married life; conscious that Bulstrode had been a benefactor to him; but was uneasy about this case; had not expected it to terminate as it had done; hardly knew how to put question to Bulstrode without appearing to insult him; if he examined housekeeper—why, the man was dead; seemed no use in implying somebody's ignorance or imprudence had killed him; and after all, he himself might be wrong
- **Return to Middlemarch with Bulstrode**: He and Bulstrode rode back to Middlemarch together, talking of many things—chiefly cholera and chances of the Reform Bill in the House of Lords, and firm resolve of political Unions; nothing was said about Raffles except that Bulstrode mentioned necessity of having grave for him in Lowick churchyard, and observed that so far as he knew, poor man had no connections except Rigg, whom he stated to be unfriendly towards him
- **Conversation with Farebrother**: Told Farebrother "Thank you for coming. I can enjoy the kindness all the more because I am happier. I have certainly been a good deal crushed"; acknowledged fear bruises will be painful later but for now torture-screw is off; disclosed plans to set up a surgery and take apprentice, saying "if Rosamond will not mind"; acknowledged having had severe galling to begin with which will make small rubs seem easy; phrase "if Rosamond will not mind" fell involuntarily as part of his thought, marking significant yoke he bore
- **Treatment Philosophy**: Strongly convinced against prevalent practice of allowing alcohol and administering large doses of opium in alcoholic poisoning cases; repeatedly acted on this conviction with favorable result
- **Medical Care of Raffles**: Gave chief instruction to Bulstrode on administration of extremely moderate doses of opium in case of sleeplessness continuing; took precaution of bringing opium in pocket; gave minute directions as to doses and point at which they should cease; insisted on risk of not ceasing; repeated order that no alcohol should be given

**Rosamond Lydgate (née Vincy)**
- Married to Lydgate; victorious obstinacy never wasting energy
- **Manipulation and Consequences**: Manipulated husband to go riding; accident at Halsell Wood led to loss of baby; regaining brilliant health
- Now possesses knowledge of Casaubon's codicil mentioning Will
- **Response to Debt Crisis**: When Lydgate proposed debt must be paid, fell like mortal chill; when presented with house-selling proposal, went to Mrs. Plymdale with congratulations instead; had secretly disobeyed by asking father for help; father said more likely to want help himself; called on Mr. Borthrop Trumbull at his office; revoked Lydgate's order before New Year's Day party
- **Written to Sir Godwin with Refusal**: Had written requesting aid; awaited answer for nearly three weeks; Sir Godwin refused all aid; stated wife should not write on business
- **Current Response to Crisis**: Told Lydgate her papa and mamma wish her to go and stay with them while things in miserable state; asked Lydgate: "Do you object, Tertius?"
- Now likely gone to stay with her parents while crisis continues

**Mr. Bulstrode**
- **Raffles's Arrival and Care**: After initial investigation of Raffles's pockets at Stone Court, found bills showing stay at inn at Bilkley (forty miles from Middlemarch), suggesting he had left portmanteau behind; Lydgate gave specific treatment instructions with moderate opium doses and strict prohibition on alcohol
- **Mental Conflict—Intention vs. Desire**: Set himself to keep intention separate from desire; inwardly declared intention to obey orders; noted how desire avails itself of irrelevant scepticism, finding larger room in every uncertainty and obscurity that looks like absence of law; still he did obey the orders
- **Evening of Care**: At six o'clock when Raffles still wakeful with fresh restlessness and perpetual cries he was sinking away, Bulstrode began administering opium according to Lydgate's directions; after half hour or more called Mrs. Abel and told her he found himself unfit for further watching; must consign patient to her care; repeated Lydgate's directions to her as to quantity of each dose; Mrs. Abel had not before known anything of Lydgate's prescriptions
- **Uncertainty About Betrayal to Caleb**: Heart sank at sign he could get no grasp over Raffles's wretched mind; could not trust any word of Raffles as to whether he had really kept silence except to Caleb Garth; housekeeper reported without constraint that since Garth left, Raffles asked for beer and after that had not spoken, seeming very ill; might be concluded there had been no betrayal; Mrs. Abel thought strange man belonged to unpleasant "kin"
- **Raffles's Death and Relief**: Raffles died during night; by morning as Bulstrode sat and beheld the enemy of his peace going irrevocably into silence, he felt more at rest than he had done for many months; his conscience was soothed by enfolding wing of secrecy, which seemed like angel sent down for his relief
- **Public Exposure of Past**: At riding past archway of Green Dragon, trusting Providence had delivered him from haunting ghost of earlier life, discovered his past has been publicly betrayed by Bambridge at the inn in Middlemarch; Bambridge heard information from "party who was old chum of Bulstrode's" (likely Raffles), picked up at Bilkley; story concerns Bulstrode's rise to fortune and involvement with pawnbroker's business; now widespread public scandal and conjecture about his past life
- **Social Consequences Beginning**: Townspeople (Mr. Hawley, Mr. Thesiger, others) turning against him; pressure mounting to force him out of parish; described as worse than men at tread-mill for his religious pretension combined with hidden past; scandal affects his standing as Bank manager and Hospital benefactor
- **Past Life and Offer to Will** (earlier): Young banker's clerk; became confidential accountant in Dunkirk's pawnbroker's business in Dunkirk; perpetual self-justification; soul saturated with belief he did everything for God's sake; wrote letter to Will; met with Will at Shrubs; when Will asked if Bulstrode connected with pawnbroker's business, Bulstrode felt suddenly uncertain and answered falteringly that Will conjectured rightly; offered five hundred pounds yearly during his life and proportional capital at death; when Will rejected money and departed with determined quickness, Bulstrode suffered violent reaction and wept
- **Plans for Change**: Change of plan determined by severe experience since Raffles recognized Will Ladislaw; banker had vainly attempted act of restitution which might move Divine Providence to arrest painful consequences; contemplates temporary withdrawal from management of much business; thinking of changing residence for a time; probably will close or let 'The Shrubs' and take place near coast under advice as to salubrity

**Mr. Raffles**
- **DECEASED as of these excerpts**: Died during night at Stone Court following Bulstrode's administration of opium
- Known to Bulstrode from twenty-five years prior; addresses him as "Nick"; claimed to be visiting stepson Joshua Rigg
- Recalled name was "Ladislaw" and wrote it down in pocket-book; deliberately decided NOT to tell Bulstrode—held secret knowledge of connection between Bulstrode and Ladislaw, intentionally concealing, treating as card to play
- Picked up by Caleb Garth in his gig after getting down from coach; recognized Caleb from previous meeting; Caleb provided shelter
- Revealed to Caleb Garth information about Bulstrode's harmful past life: that Bulstrode led harmful life for gain, kept others out of their rights by deceit
- **Final State**: Showed intense vague terror; deprecated Bulstrode's anger; claimed money all gone, robbed; said came because ill and somebody hunting him; told nobody anything, kept mouth shut; consciousness interrupted; had only fitful perturbed snatches of sleep; waked with fresh restlessness and perpetual cries that he was sinking away; would take hardly any food, persistently wakeful and restlessly raving but not violent; took little notice of Lydgate's presence
- **Betrayal of Bulstrode's Secrets**: Before death, disclosed Bulstrode's pawnbroker past and financial maneuverings to Bambridge at Bilkley (PLAN/CLAIM—account given by Bambridge); this information now public in Middlemarch

**Mr. Farebrother (Vicar)**
- Aware Lydgate is proud man; had been playing whist to satisfy mother
- **Intervention with Fred and Mary**: Left whist-table to speak with Lydgate, disclosing Lydgate had done him service by influencing him to stop playing for money; later approached Fred at billiard-table; confessed temptation to let Fred ruin himself; disclosed satisfaction of Fred's affections stands in way of his own; warned Mary's affection is "conditionally bound"; claimed another man might win firm place through companionship of ready sympathy; overcame temptation to act selfishly
- **Response to Lydgate's Beneficence**: When Lydgate mentioned Bulstrode's financial aid, Farebrother compelled himself to approve of man whom he disliked; delicate feeling shrank from dwelling even in thought on fact that he had always urged Lydgate to avoid personal entanglement with Bulstrode; said Bulstrode must naturally feel interest in Lydgate's welfare after he worked with him in way reducing his income; glad to think Bulstrode has acted accordingly
- Watching Mary Garth with evident admiration while she tells Rumpelstiltskin tale
